name: The Oak of Tombeboeuf

location.address: Rural field off the road toward Laperche, about 8km northwest of Tombeboeuf, Lot-et-Garonne, France (near GPS N44 32.788 E0 26.056)

access: On private agricultural land; the tourism board's own current listing states 'Visite libre' (free, self-guided visit, no booking or permission needed). It stands alone in an open field and is hard to find without directions; the tourist board publishes a contact (CPIE47, +33 5 53 88 83 30) for visitor guidance rather than requiring it.
transport: No public transport; reached by car, roughly 8km outside Tombeboeuf village.
container: new place: standalone. No published city nearby (Agen is roughly 50km away). A genuine Tree of the Year 2019 winner with real fame and a dramatic solitary silhouette. Rechecked 2026-09-05: the tourism board's current page lists 'Visite libre' with no access restriction, and a March 2025 article discusses the tree in the present tense with no distress noted, together treated as sufficient evidence the tree survived its 2022 crisis. Ships under the single-tree-destination exception.
story:
In 2019 France gave its Tree of the Year title to an oak standing on its own in a field. It sits on high ground about eight kilometres outside Tombeboeuf, with no signpost and no path to it, which is why the departmental tourist board publishes a telephone number for visitor guidance rather than directions.

The two accounts of the tree do not agree. The tourist board puts it at roughly 300 years, 6.30 metres round and 25 metres tall. A specialist tree blog that walked out to it in 2008 called it young at 250 and paid more attention to its shape: the first branches leave the trunk about three metres up and then travel sideways rather than up, which is what an oak does when nothing near it competes for light. The ARBRES association had already labelled it a Remarkable Tree in 2003.

In February 2022 a large fissure opened in the trunk and local residents and environmental groups worried it might not survive the weight of a new season's leaves. A restoration campaign followed. Nothing published since names the tree as lost, and the tourist board's current listing still describes it in the present tense with no mention of ongoing danger, so it is treated here as having come through it, though nobody has published an explicit all-clear.

The field is private agricultural land, and the tourist board's own current listing calls it a free, self-guided visit, no booking required. Nobody has settled which oak it is, either. If you can read the leaf, say so.

name: The Millennial Yew of Yvignac-la-Tour

location.address: Beside the church, Yvignac-la-Tour, Cotes-d'Armor, Brittany, France

access: Free, standing beside the parish church; ordinary churchyard access.
transport: No station; reached by car, near Dinan in Cotes-d'Armor.
verify_notes: Believed to date from when a chapel on the site became the parish church, somewhere in the 7th to 11th century, so treat the 'thousand years' figure as the source's own loose estimate rather than a precise date; some local sources connect the Breton word 'if' (yew) to the town's own name. Girth 8.5m (850cm) measured at 1m height, per krapooarboricole's visit. The tree is hollow and visibly declining but still described as having 'a reasonably harmonious form'; the commune planted a successor yew beside it in December 2000, which is itself a sign the original was already recognised as failing over two decades ago and is being actively stewarded rather than neglected. Local tradition holds a refractory priest, Guillaume Gauvain (d.1794, French Revolution), is buried beneath its roots. No tree-level coordinate found in this pass; the lead's own lat/lng were null, and I could not confirm a coordinate against a mapped source, so location stays approximate (behind/beside the church only).
container: new place: standalone. No published city nearby (Dinan has no page). A genuinely ancient, well-documented churchyard yew with real local history (Revolutionary-era burial legend, name etymology); clears the single-tree-destination bar on age and story, though a follow-up should try to pin an exact coordinate and find a post-2010 condition check.
